components.cost_effect: Snapshot costs n gradients per epoch; caching determines the 1.5 versus 2.5 amortized count and memory. Option I uses two proximal calls per iteration.
components.goal: Control estimator variance while coupling proximal gradient and mirror steps.
components.key_estimate: Source Lemma 2.4, p.11: E||v-grad f(x)||^2<=2L[f(tilde_x)-f(x)-<grad f(x),tilde_x-x>]. Lemmas 2.6–2.7, pp.12–13, cancel the associated inner-product term through the three-point mixture.
components.name: Snapshot control variate and negative momentum
components.operation: Use the three-point x mixture with tau2=1/2, exact snapshot full gradient, and the same indexed component at current x and snapshot, followed by the two exact proximal updates.
components.requires: Component convexity and L-smoothness, uniform index sampling, exact snapshot gradient and sigma-strong convexity of psi.
transfer_checks: Re-establish unbiasedness and Lemma 2.4 after changing sampling or estimator.
Re-establish coupling and epoch telescoping after changing weights, momentum, norm, psi curvature or prox accuracy.

content.family: Katyusha negative momentum with variance reduction and proximal linear coupling

limitations.statement: Full snapshot gradients and two exact proximal minimizations are required; a generic unbiased stochastic-gradient oracle alone does not realize this protocol.
Option II, arbitrary sampling, non-Euclidean geometry, approximate prox, last-iterate output, nonuniform smoothness and sparse implementation are outside this selected certification.

performance_links.scope_note: Only Option I under the complete conditions of thm.P021.katyusha_rate; no unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound.

variants.cost: Per epoch, compute n component gradients for mu^s. Caching all n snapshot gradients requires O(nd) storage in general and m further component gradients per epoch: total S(n+m)=3nS, or 1.5 amortized per inner iteration for m=2n. Without caching, require 2m further component gradients: total S(n+2m)=5nS, or 2.5 amortized, with O(d) vector state. Option I separately requires 2mS exact proximal evaluations, one at each scale per inner iteration; their psi-dependent arithmetic cost is not included in gradient counts. Dense vector combinations and incremental weighted accumulation require O(d) arithmetic per inner iteration and O(d) work vectors. No sparse implementation is certified here.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.9 Algorithm 1 lines 1–16, Option I; pp.9–10 Remark 2.2 and footnote 11.
variants.name: Algorithm 1 Option I, Euclidean strongly convex case
variants.output: Return tilde_x^S, the geometrically weighted final-epoch average of y iterates; return x0 if S=0. The selected performance does not certify last-y or last-query output.
public_inputs: n and access to every indexed component gradient
x0 with finite F(x0), and nonnegative integer epoch count S
Known L>0 bounding every component smoothness and known sigma>0 strong convexity parameter of psi
Exact prox_{t psi}(u)=argmin_z{||z-u||^2/(2t)+psi(z)} at t=alpha and t=1/(3L)
variants.query_and_update: For s=0,...,S-1 compute mu^s=(1/n)sum_i grad f_i(tilde_x^s). For j=0,...,m-1, k=sm+j: set x_{k+1}=tau1*z_k+tau2*tilde_x^s+(1-tau1-tau2)*y_k; draw uniform i and form v=mu^s+grad f_i(x_{k+1})-grad f_i(tilde_x^s). Set z_{k+1}=argmin_z{||z-z_k||^2/(2alpha)+<v,z>+psi(z)} and y_{k+1}=argmin_y{(3L/2)||y-x_{k+1}||^2+<v,y>+psi(y)}. Set tilde_x^{s+1}=(sum_{j=0}^{m-1}theta^j*y_{sm+j+1})/(sum_{j=0}^{m-1}theta^j).
variants.requirements: On Euclidean R^d, F=(1/n)sum_i f_i+psi; n,d positive integers; every f_i convex and L-smooth; psi convex, lower semicontinuous and sigma-strongly convex; minimizer exists. Use exact gradients and proximal minimizations, with a fresh uniform component index conditional on the past at every inner iteration.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set m=2n, tau2=1/2, tau1=min{sqrt(m*sigma/(3L)),1/2}, alpha=1/(3*tau1*L), theta=1+alpha*sigma. Initialize y0=z0=tilde_x^0=x0. Carry y,z across epochs without resetting.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Run exactly S epochs with the stated fixed parameters. Algorithm 1 has no objective-based stopping test. Accuracy scheduling uses Theorem 2.1's two-case bound; its O-notation does not specify a numerical prefactor. Scheduling from log(Delta0/epsilon) requires a valid initial-gap bound and sufficiently large constant; supplying S directly needs no Delta0.
